Following the release of iOS 26.6, iPadOS 26.6 and related software updates, Apple has detailed the massive security patch contents included in today's new system versions.

The iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6 security updates have widespread impact on iPhone and iPad

In iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, Apple provides over 75 security patches for iPhone and iPad, covering multiple areas of the system.

More specifically, Apple's security advisory contains 78 individual vulnerability entries, involving 87 unique CVE numbers. Since some entries involve more than one CVE, the number of CVEs is higher.

Apple has not indicated that any of the vulnerabilities patched in iOS 26.6 have been maliciously exploited.

Among Apple's lengthy list, several patches stand out:

  • A vulnerability in MediaRemote may allow an application to obtain root privileges.
  • A vulnerability in AVEVideoEncoder may allow an application to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges.
  • Vulnerabilities in Game Center and libc may allow malicious applications to bypass sandbox restrictions.
  • A vulnerability in CloudAttestation may allow malicious applications to bypass code signature enforcement.
  • A vulnerability in ImageIO may lead to arbitrary code execution when processing specially crafted malicious images.
  • Three vulnerabilities in SceneKit may lead to arbitrary code execution when processing specially crafted malicious files.
  • An accessibility feature issue may leak sensitive data through iPhone Mirroring to individuals with physical access.
  • A vulnerability in Contacts may allow an application to add contacts without user authorisation.

Kernel, WebKit and Wi-Fi patches

Apple has also patched over a dozen kernel vulnerabilities. Potential impacts include corrupting or writing kernel memory, leaking kernel memory, bypassing network filters, and causing the system to terminate unexpectedly.

WebKit has also received a large number of patches. These vulnerabilities may expose process memory, leak whether a user has visited specific links, allow interface spoofing, violate iframe sandbox rules, allow applications to read files outside their sandbox, or cause Safari to crash.

Another Wi-Fi vulnerability may allow nearby attackers to corrupt process memory.

Beyond the 78 documented security patches, Apple includes an "Additional Acknowledgements" section, listing 12 acknowledgements.

These entries are intended to thank researchers for their assistance, but are not listed as independent security patches and have not been assigned additional CVE numbers.

The complete patch list and researcher acknowledgements have been published on Apple's website.

Security patches for Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV and Apple Vision Pro

Apple's newly released macOS Tahoe 26.6 security advisory lists 155 unique CVEs.

Beyond several patches shared with iPhone and iPad, the Mac update also addresses multiple vulnerabilities, including ones that may allow applications to obtain root privileges, escape the sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper checks or privacy preferences, and access protected data.

Apple also released security updates for older versions of macOS on the same day, though they are not included in this article's statistics.

Apple has also detailed the patch contents for watchOS 26.6, tvOS 26.6 and visionOS 26.6. After subtracting cross-platform overlaps, Apple's latest updates collectively address 194 unique CVEs.

Apple previously stated that, to counter AI-driven attack tools, it has accelerated the pace of security patch releases and brought forward last month's iOS 26.5.2 update.
